title: Hedra Automation: Setup Guide and Pricing (2026)
summary: Hedra automation starts video generation from outside the studio. The fastest method uses a script or Activepieces to trigger API calls automatically.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Does Hedra have an official API?


Yes, and it's the route this article recommends: you submit a generation request, wait for the render, and download the result, all without opening the editor. Use it in preference to browser scripting, which breaks whenever the interface changes.


Confirm the current endpoints and authentication in Hedra's own API documentation before you build, because I haven't reproduced every call here.


### Can I automate Hedra without coding?


Yes, if your automation tool can send an HTTP request with a custom header and read a field from the response. That covers the trigger, submit, check status and download steps.


Usually the trouble is the status check, which needs a loop with a stop condition. Without one, a stuck job keeps your workflow running and your credits draining. Test the loop on one clip before you point it at a batch.


### How much does Hedra automation cost per video?


You don't pay for the API call itself. Each render consumes credits, and the amount depends on your plan and on what you ask for.


Rather than quote a rate that may be out of date, run one representative clip, read the balance before and after, and multiply. Failed and retried jobs count toward that figure, so include them in your estimate.


### Why does my Hedra generation keep failing?


In most failures I would trace, the cause is one of three: an exhausted credit balance, a plan limit on simultaneous renders, or a malformed input such as an unsupported file. The symptom is usually a job that never completes, not a clear error.


Check the balance and your concurrency headroom first, then the input. Log every attempt so you can see which cause you are dealing with.


### Can I use automated Hedra videos commercially?


That depends on your plan's terms, not on whether a human or a script pressed the button. Read the current terms for your tier before publishing paid or client work.


Four questions remain unsettled by the body, each last checked on 21 November 2026:


- Commercial use: governed by plan terms, so read your tier's terms before you ship client work.
- Concurrency on Basic: no confirmed limit, so test by submitting parallel jobs and watching for rejections or queueing.
- Credit expiry: unconfirmed, so check your account page and avoid stockpiling credits you can't verify.
- Webhooks versus polling: polling is the documented path I can vouch for, and I haven't confirmed webhook support.


Treat each as something to verify against your own account, then record the result and its date next to your workflow.
